title: 'Suicidal' man dies as police try to arrest him: Chris James Eklund, 41, was despondent over the death of his mother
article: Vancouver police are investigating the death of an apparently suicidal man who died after getting into a struggle with officers trying to subdue him.

Constable Sarah Bloor said the incident happened at 11 p.m. Thursday when police received a call about a suicidal man in a third- floor apartment of what was described as his temporary home in the 900-block Jervis.
She said at least two police officers arrived to find Chris James Eklund, 41, very despondent about the recent death of his mother.

She said they tried to take Eklund into custody under the Mental Health Act, but a struggle ensued in the apartment. Eklund, who was described as a large, obese man who was intoxicated at the time, collapsed. Attempts were made to resuscitate him, but he died at the scene.
Bloor said police don't know why Eklund died, but an autopsy was to be conducted Friday.
She said police are treating the matter as a death in custody, meaning the major crime squad will conduct the investigation.

Bloor said there is no indication Eklund had any weapons at the time. "He indicated he was suicidal and he was despondent over the death of his mother. I don't know how he was going to effect the suicide, but he indicated he was going to cause harm to himself.
"\[The officers\] were trying to get him medical treatment. He didn't want that."
Bloor said additional police were called to help once he started fighting with the two officers.
She also said there was no indication police used a choke hold to subdue the man. "It's unfortunate."
